title: Rabbi Yehoshua bar Abba
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In Shabbat 126 and Moed Katan 5b he speaks in Ulla’s name; in Bava Batra 15 and Menachot 30, in Rav Gidel’s name in Rav’s name. In Yoma 42b he raises a difficulty, which Abaye calls a refutation; this suggests that he preceded Abaye. His consistent title Rabbi suggests that he was Palestinian and studied there with Ulla and Rav Gidel, who later also lived in the Land of Israel. Seder HaDorot cites him in Zevachim 32b, but our reading there is Rav Hoshaya.

notes.text: ירושלמי here is rendered Palestinian, without asserting residence specifically in Jerusalem. The Hoshaya reading is Hyman’s reported variant.

The consulted Yoma 42b separately supplies Yehoshua bar Abba’s objection and Abaye’s explanation. The relative chronology and Palestinian education inferred from these reports and the consistent title Rabbi remain Hyman’s conclusions.
